name: Andong Station Downtown
description: The area around Andong Station and the nearby Ok-dong shopping streets is the city's real center of daily life, packed with cafes, jjimdak restaurants, banks, and the main bus routes out to Hahoe and Dosan Seowon. It's the most convenient base for remote workers who need reliable wifi cafes and easy transit access, though English signage remains sparse.
bestFor: remote workers wanting cafes, transit, and daily errands within walking distance
pros: Best cafe wifi options in the city

name: Hahoe Folk Village
tagline: A living UNESCO village on a bend of the Nakdong
description: Set inside a horseshoe curve of the Nakdong River about 40 minutes from downtown by bus, Hahoe is a preserved clan village of traditional thatched and tile-roofed hanok houses still inhabited by descendants of the Ryu clan. It's home to the Hahoe mask dance tradition and draws day-trippers rather than long-stay residents, but a short stay in a village guesthouse offers a rare, immersive traditional-Korea experience.
bestFor: cultural immersion, photography, short traditional-stay experiences
pros: Home of the mask dance tradition
cons: Bus ride from downtown, not walkable from the city center
Very limited services, no real workspace options

name: Wolyeonggyo Riverside
tagline: The city's scenic wooden bridge and evening promenade
description: Wolyeonggyo, a long reconstructed wooden pedestrian bridge crossing the Nakdong River near downtown, anchors a pleasant riverside park popular for evening walks, cycling, and photos, especially when the bridge is lit up after dark. It's close enough to central Andong to be a regular after-work walk rather than a special trip, and it sits near several riverside restaurants and cafes.
bestFor: evening walks, cycling, and unwinding after a work day
cons: Limited food options right on the riverside itself
Quiet and sparsely lit outside the bridge area

name: Dosan Seowon and Old Town
tagline: Confucian academy country north of the city
description: Dosan Seowon, one of Korea's most important Confucian academies, sits among pine forest above the Nakdong River roughly 30 to 40 minutes north of downtown, alongside other historic clan villages and study halls tied to the philosopher Yi Hwang. This area is more rural retreat than neighborhood, best suited to day trips for those wanting a deep look at Korea's academic and Confucian heritage.
bestFor: history and philosophy-minded travelers seeking quiet, scenic day trips
cons: Requires a car or infrequent bus for access
Essentially no dining or lodging infrastructure nearby
